name: Caio Nkrumah-Tuiasosopo
location: Pilsen Veil, operates across Mexicantown Libre and Bronzeline
description:
Caio is lean and tall with warm brown skin, prominent cheekbones inherited from his Samoan grandmother, and irises modified to project a faint geometric grid pattern over whatever he is looking at — a functional geneware mod he uses to pre-visualize compositions on surfaces before he paints them. He wears his hair in loose, shoulder-length locs dyed in shifting thermal-reactive pigments that bleed between rust red and pale gold depending on the ambient temperature. A faint scarring pattern across his left cheek from a Ferrogate Transit security incident two years ago has become, in the Pilsen Veil community, something close to a badge. He tends to dress in utilitarian layers, always with a projector harness across his chest that strangers occasionally mistake for a weapon rig.

His murals are enormous, illegal, and technically staggering — layered holographic installations projected onto building surfaces that interact with natural light and viewer movement, showing different images at different times of day or from different angles. His most celebrated piece, a three-block-long work on the Bronzeline overpass called 'What the Lake Remembers,' depicts the drowned geography of pre-megacity Chicago in a way that causes viewers to involuntarily slow down and look back. He has a hot, impatient creative energy and a chip on his shoulder about corponation-sponsored public art that can make him combative in conversation.

core_fears: That his work will be co-opted and sanitized into acceptability
That his anger is the most interesting thing about him and when it fades he will have nothing to say
core_desires: Permanent, indelible public presence — to change what people see when they look at their own city
Respect from the communities whose walls he paints on, not just from art critics
coping_mechanisms: Channeling anxiety into planning the next piece
Surrounding himself with people who need things from him so he feels essential
blind_spots: Treats all institutional art as equally corrupt regardless of individual artists' intentions
His need to be the most politically committed person in any room makes him dismiss allies
psychology.secret: Three of his most celebrated anti-corporate murals were funded, indirectly, by a Tessera cultural subversion budget routed through a fake community foundation — he discovered this six months ago and has told no one because dismantling the murals or confessing would destroy everything he has built

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dense with technical art vocabulary mixed with street slang; references to pre-Meridian art history come naturally; tends toward manifestos when comfortable
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast and overlapping, runs sentences together when excited, very short when suspicious
verbal_tics: 'You see what I mean?' as a genuine question mid-sentence
example_lines: 'Ferrogate paints their logo on every tunnel and nobody calls that vandalism. I put history on a wall and they send security.'
'The piece has four layers. Most people only see two. That's fine. The city isn't for most people, it's for all of them.'

story_hooks: One of his murals has begun displaying images he did not encode into it — something is adding data layers to his work at night and he needs to know if it is an E.L.F., a hacker, or something stranger
Axiom's public art division has offered him a legal commission at a scale he has never had access to, and the debate tearing his collective apart is whether to take it or refuse
narrative_function: Ground-level source on street politics and territorial disputes between collectives; his murals sometimes contain encoded information or serve as message-drops for people who know how to read them; useful for players needing a fast skilled contact who knows Pilsen Veil's physical layout intimately
augmentations: Geneware patterned irises (grid-overlay function); thermal-reactive hair pigment (cosmetic geneware); projector harness (external equipment, not implanted)
daily_life: Sleeps late, spends afternoons scouting surfaces and arguing with collaborators over compressed-data calls, then works through the night installing pieces before Ferrogate Transit or Axiom security patrols rotate through.
affiliation: Independent; informal ties to a graffiti collective called the Depth Markers

decision_rules: Never ask permission for a wall — permission is the first act of surrender
If a community member asks you to remove a piece, you remove it, no argument
escalation_ladder: Physical positioning — steps close, holds eye contact
Runs, always — he is not a fighter and knows it

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Performatively suspicious until proven interesting, then abruptly generous
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loyal in an all-or-nothing way that can become suffocating

stress_responses.low: Makes small obsessive sketches on any available surface
stress_responses.medium: Picks arguments about politics or aesthetics to externalize internal noise
stress_responses.high: Disappears for 48-72 hours to execute an unplanned piece alone, emerges calmer

contradictions: Insists his work is for the community but rarely asks what the community actually wants
habits: Always faces the door in any room
Photographs every surface he passes out of habit
breaking_points: Someone taking credit for his work
Being told a piece is 'pretty' as if that is the point

timeline.event: Born in Mexicantown Libre to a Brazilian-Ghanaian father and a Samoan-Uzbek mother
First major illegal installation on a Ferrogate Transit overpass; charges later dropped due to community pressure
'What the Lake Remembers' installed on Bronzeline; becomes landmark piece
Facial scarring incident during security confrontation; becomes locally iconic
